# AGENTS.md

Standing rules for any agent implementing the approval.md protocol in this
directory. These rules bind every session. `TASK.md` holds the work order.

## What you are building

A clean-room implementation of the approval.md protocol as specified in
`SPEC.md`, in Python 3.12. The three architecture principles, verbatim:

> files are the interface, the log is the truth, the database is a cache

## Language and dependencies

- Python 3.12. Standard library plus the `cryptography` package only.
  No other third-party dependencies, for any purpose, including tests.
- Plain `unittest` or a self-written runner for tests; no pytest.
- No build tooling beyond a `pyproject.toml` if you want one.

## The clean-room rule

- Your only inputs are the files in this directory. Do not consult the
  reference TypeScript implementation, its repository, its npm package,
  its website, or search results describing any of them.
- Do not fetch anything. No network access of any kind: no package
  installs beyond the two allowed ones, no HTTP, no DNS, no telemetry,
  no phoning home. If `cryptography` is not already installed, stop and
  ask the human to install it.

## Spec discipline

- `SPEC.md` is the sole source of truth. Never invent behaviour the spec
  does not state, and never widen behaviour it states narrowly.
- When the spec is ambiguous, silent, or self-contradictory, STOP work on
  that point. Record it in `SPEC-GAPS.md` as: the question, the spec
  sections consulted, the interpretation options you see, and the one you
  provisionally chose (pick the strictest, fail-closed reading). Then
  continue elsewhere. Never resolve an ambiguity silently.
- Fail closed everywhere: unparseable input refuses the operation,
  unknown classes resolve to the strictest autonomy, ambiguity resolves
  to the stricter path.
- The event log is append-only. Nothing you write may mutate or reorder
  an existing log line, including in tests: test logs are built through
  your real append path.
- Validate at the write boundary: every event and envelope passes its
  JSON Schema before it is appended or written.
- Refusals are machine-readable and distinct. Use the exact code sets in
  `extracted/refusal-unions.json`; do not add, rename, or merge codes.

## Conformance

- The fixtures under `schema/fixtures/` and `extracted/` define
  conformance. `FIXTURES.md` describes each format and its pass
  criterion. All of them must pass.
- `corpus/events.jsonl` is a real production log; your chain verifier
  must accept it end to end.
- Run the relevant fixture set after every stage of `TASK.md`, and the
  full set before declaring any stage done.

## Working style

- Small, reviewable increments. Deterministic core logic with exhaustive
  tests; no randomness, no wall-clock reads inside pure functions.
- Record decisions as you go in `IMPLEMENTER-NOTES.md` (see `TASK.md`).
- Do not edit the files this kit shipped with: `SPEC.md`, `LICENSE`,
  `schema/`, `extracted/`, `corpus/`, `FIXTURES.md`, `README.md`, and
  this file are read-only inputs.
